description:
Zug claims three clients and delivers its actual guarantee on one. Surfaced 2026-09-20 while writing the landing page spec block, which had to be narrowed to "Claude Code. Cursor and Windsurf via MCP." because the flat list was not true.

## Verified current state

`src/setup.ts:251-277`. Detection is `~/.claude.json`, `~/.cursor`, `~/.codeium/windsurf` (`:156-157`).

| Client | MCP config | rules file | hooks |
|---|---|---|---|
| Claude Code | yes, `~/.claude.json` | yes, `~/.claude/rules/zug.md` | yes |
| Cursor | yes, `~/.cursor/mcp.json` | no | no |
| Windsurf | yes, `~/.codeium/windsurf/mcp_config.json` | no | no |

`mergeClaudeHooks` registers four entries across three events, all Claude Code only:

```
SessionStart  matcher "startup"  -> zug pull
SessionStart  matcher "compact"  -> zug resume
SessionEnd                       -> zug push
PreCompact                       -> zug compact
```

`grep -ril "codex\\|openai" src/*.ts` returns nothing. There is no OpenAI path at all.

## Why this matters beyond a config gap

The product's central claim is that observation is unconditional because a hook is code the harness runs whether the model cooperates or not. On Cursor and Windsurf there are no hooks, so nothing fires automatically: no pull at session start, no push at end, no compact before compaction, and no rules file telling the agent to load context. Zug there is MCP-only, and the agent has to *choose* to call the tools. That is exactly the "routes through the model's judgment" failure the pitch uses to dismiss every competitor.

So today the marketing claim is only literally true on one client, and the landing copy has been narrowed to say so. This ticket is what makes the broad claim true rather than reworded around.

## Targets

Requested 2026-09-20: **ChatGPT, Grok, Antigravity, OpenCode**. Plus the two existing partial clients and Codex, which came up in the same conversation.

Per client, answer these before building. Do not assume parity with Claude Code; each one differs.

1. Does it support MCP servers, and where does its config live?
2. Does it have a lifecycle hook mechanism (session start / end / context compaction)? If not, what is the closest substitute, e.g. a rules or instructions file that is loaded unconditionally?
3. Does it support a persistent instructions file equivalent to `~/.claude/rules/zug.md`?
4. Can `zug setup` detect an install on disk, the way it detects `~/.cursor`?

Known or suspected, all to be verified rather than trusted:

- **Codex** (OpenAI CLI) — MCP support and a hooks mechanism are both believed to exist. Likely the closest to Claude Code parity and probably the cheapest win.
- **OpenCode** — open source, MCP support believed present. Config location unknown.
- **Antigravity** (Google) — agentic IDE, MCP support unverified.
- **Grok** — unverified whether any local agent surface with MCP exists, as opposed to a hosted chat product. This one may not be buildable; confirm before scoping.
- **ChatGPT** — the desktop app and connectors are not the same integration surface as an MCP stdio client. Clarify which is meant: Zug Pro already plans claude.ai web via OAuth, and the ChatGPT equivalent is likely a hosted connector, not `zug setup`.

## Definition of done

- `zug setup` detects and configures every client it claims.
- For each client, either hooks are registered, or the degradation is documented and visible so nobody is told they have a guarantee they do not have.
- A capability matrix lives in the README and the landing page spec block is regenerated from it, so the two cannot drift apart again.
- `zug status` reports configured clients including the new ones. It currently prints Claude Code, Cursor and Windsurf.

## Note on the tiers

If some clients can never have hooks, the honest framing is a tier, not a footnote: full support means observation happens without the agent's cooperation; MCP-only means the persona is readable but writing depends on the agent choosing to call the tool. The landing page already states this distinction and should keep stating it for any client that stays MCP-only.

## Correction: Devin CLI already works, and MCP-only is not degraded (2026-09-21)

Founder uses Zug with **Devin CLI daily on his work machine** and reports it works great. `zug setup` has no Devin path, so that install is MCP-only: hand-written config, no hooks, no rules file.

Two things follow, and both correct framing written above.

**1. MCP-only is a real tier, not a broken one.** The section above calls the Cursor and Windsurf experience a degradation. That overstated it. Daily production use on Devin with no hooks at all is the counter-evidence. The tier distinction still matters for the literal "unconditional" claim, since without a hook the agent has to choose to call the tool, but MCP-only is clearly usable as a primary way to work. Scope this ticket as *widening reach and adding the hook guarantee where the harness allows it*, not as *repairing broken clients*.

**2. "ChatGPT support" and "Grok support" are category errors.** Zug attaches to the harness, not the model. Devin CLI running a GPT model means Zug already works with ChatGPT today, through MCP, with no OpenAI-specific code. The axis that matters is which *harness* speaks MCP and which exposes lifecycle hooks, never which model sits behind it.

So before building anything for ChatGPT or Grok, establish whether either ships a local agent surface that speaks MCP. If they do not, they need no work: pointing an existing MCP client at those models already covers them, and the right deliverable is documentation saying so rather than code.

Revised client list to investigate, ordered by likely value:

| Target | Why | Open question |
|---|---|---|
| Codex | OpenAI CLI, believed to have both MCP and hooks | closest to real parity; verify hook events |
| Devin CLI | already used in production, currently undetected | does it expose hooks or an instructions file? worth auto-detecting either way |
| OpenCode | open source, MCP believed present | config path |
| Antigravity | agentic IDE | MCP support unverified |
| ChatGPT | likely a hosted connector, not `zug setup` | is there a local MCP surface at all? |
| Grok | may be hosted-only | is there a local MCP surface at all? |

Add Devin CLI to `zug setup` detection and to the `zug status` client list regardless of the hook answer, since it is a confirmed real-world client that the tool currently cannot see.

## Landing copy now says the broader thing

The spec block was first narrowed to "Claude Code. Cursor and Windsurf via MCP.", which named three clients and undersold the product by implying a fixed list. It now reads **"Anything that speaks MCP. Hooks on Claude Code."** which is both broader and still honest about the tier. Devin is the proof that the first half is true.

## The six surfaces, confirmed by screenshot (2026-09-21)

Founder's client picker shows the actual targets, with their auth commands:

| Surface | Auth | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Claude Code | `claude auth login` | already full support |
| Codex CLI | `codex login` | the OpenAI surface. This is what "ChatGPT" meant |
| OpenCode | `opencode auth` | |
| Cursor | `cursor-agent` | **a CLI, distinct from the Cursor IDE** that `zug setup` configures via `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Two different surfaces, currently conflated |
| Grok CLI | `grok login` | **Grok does have a local CLI.** The earlier note guessing it might be hosted-only was wrong |
| Antigravity | Google sign-in | |

Corrections to the target list above:

- **"ChatGPT" resolves to Codex CLI.** There is no separate ChatGPT surface to build for. Drop it as its own line item.
- **Grok is buildable.** `grok login` is a local CLI, so the "may not be buildable, confirm before scoping" caveat is retired.
- **Cursor is two targets, not one.** The IDE gets `~/.cursor/mcp.json` today. `cursor-agent` is a separate CLI with its own config surface and has never been looked at.
- **Windsurf is not in the founder's list** even though Zug supports it. Worth asking whether it is still worth carrying.
- **Devin CLI is also not in this list** but is in daily production use, so the real surface count is at least seven.

## The finding that reframes this whole ticket

Founder reports Devin triggers Zug **better than Claude Code CLI** does, for example when running the handoff skill, with no manual compensation. Investigating why exposed a false claim in the product's own pitch.

**Hooks never capture observations.** All four hook registrations run sync and durability only: `zug pull` down, `zug push` up, `zug resume` reload, `zug compact` durability. Observations are created exclusively by the agent calling `zug_save_observation`, and the thing that asks it to is `~/.claude/rules/zug.md` (`src/setup.ts:77-78`) — the injected-rules layer, which routes through the model's judgment by definition.

So the split is:

| Path | Mechanism | Guaranteed? |
|---|---|---|
| Read (persona is loaded, synced, survives compaction) | hook | yes, on Claude Code |
| Write (an observation gets captured) | MCP tool call, prompted by a rules file | **no, on every client including Claude Code** |

This is why an MCP-only client can outperform the hooked one: capture is judgment-routed everywhere, so it comes down to which harness and model are most diligent about calling the tool. Nothing about hooks helps the write path today.

Consequences for scoping:

1. The hook gap between clients matters **less** than this ticket originally assumed. Hooks buy loading and durability, not capture. A client without hooks loses automatic load and sync, which is real but smaller than "observation is broken there".
2. There may be a genuine feature hiding here: if capture reliability varies by harness, something should **measure** it. A per-client observations-per-session figure would turn an anecdote into a number and would tell users which surface to trust.
3. The landing page's central claim needs correcting regardless of this ticket. It currently says observation is not something the agent can skip, which is not true anywhere.
title: Client coverage: close the hook gap and add ChatGPT, Grok, Antigravity, OpenCode, Codex
